Rules / Formatting

SK0219 A namespace-qualified reference is not shortened

skala arrange would drop a namespace qualifier, or a global::, that the reference does not need under skala_prefer_qualified_reference = false.

CategoryFormatting
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

A qualifier tells the reader that the short name would have meant something else. Where it would not — new System.Text.StringBuilder() beside using System.Text; — the qualifier is noise, and an AI-written file carries it in every position. The rule binds the shortened name at the reference's own position and rewrites only when it reaches the same type, so a shadowed or ambiguous name keeps its qualifier.

Example

Instead of:

using System.Text;

var builder = new System.Text.StringBuilder();

Write:

using System.Text;

var builder = new StringBuilder();

When it does not fire

Never adds a using: a name whose namespace is not imported stays qualified. Never shortens part-way (RegularExpressions.Regex is never written) and never uses an alias. Documentation crefs, using and namespace declarations, extern aliases, explicit interface specifiers, comments inside the name and formatter-off regions are left alone. A global:: whose name cannot lose its namespace loses only the global::. A using the shortened name now binds through is kept even if it was unused when the pass began.

Configuration

  • skala_prefer_qualified_reference
